blocks.text: [F] Control Print makes industrial coding and marking printers (continuous inkjet, thermal inkjet, high-resolution, laser, thermal transfer overprinters, large character printers, hot coders) and sells the inks, solvents, spares and service that keep them running on customer production lines (AR2026 p.42). [F] Manufacturing sits at two owned plants: Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh (about 30,000 sq ft; CIJ, LCP, TTO and hot coders) and Guwahati, Assam (about 70,000 sq ft; TIJ, hi-res printers, inks and solvents) (AR2026 p.15). [MC] It calls itself the only Indian company among the four players that hold nearly 80% of an Indian coding and marking market of about Rs 2,000-2,200 crore, with an 18-20% share of organised players (PPT Jul 2026; AR2026 p.22).

[F] The model is razor-and-blade. In FY26 the coding and marking revenue split was printers 14%, consumables 61%, spares 9% and services 15% (CALL May 2026). [MC] Management says printers stay on a line for seven to eight years and pull consumables throughout (AR2026 p.43). [MC] The installed base is put at 22,000+ printers in the annual report (AR2026 p.6) and 23,000+ in the July 2026 presentation (PPT Jul 2026); 3,064 printers were sold in FY26 and 574 in Q1 FY27 (CALL May 2026; CALL Jul 2026).

[F] End markets: the company names pipes and extruded plastics, food, dairy, cable and wire, FMCG, steel and metal, wood/plywood, cement, sugar and healthcare as its main verticals (AR2026 p.45). [F] No percentage split by end market is disclosed; management describes the industrial side (pipes, cable, steel) as the larger and more cyclical part, and packaging (food, beverage, personal care, pharma) as steadier (CALL May 2026). [MC] Extrusion is described as the single biggest consumables user (CALL Jul 2026).

[F] Geography: the standalone entity is almost entirely domestic, with exports at 2.46% of standalone turnover in FY26 (AR2026 p.75). [F] The five foreign subsidiaries (Control Print BV, Markprint BV, Codeology Group, CP Italy, Control Print MEA FZE) had combined revenue of Rs 34.81 crore and a combined net loss of Rs 31.24 crore in FY26 (AR2026 p.206). [E] That is about 7% of FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 482 crore before inter-company eliminations (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.206).

[F] Customers are corporate manufacturers only, with no dealers or distributors (AR2026 p.87). [F] CRISIL names Ashirvad Pipes, Supreme Industries, Tata Steel, Finolex Industries, Sudhakar PVC Products, Hindustan Unilever, Britannia, Hindware and KEI Industries among clients (RATING). [F] Customer concentration figures (top 1 / 5 / 10) are not disclosed anywhere in the documents.

[F] Listing status: the company was incorporated on 14 January 1991 and is listed on BSE (522295) and NSE (CONTROLPR) (AR2026 p.74). [AI] This is a long-listed company, not a recent IPO, so there is no prospectus and none was provided. The evidence base is one annual report, four call transcripts, one presentation, one credit rating rationale and screener.in data.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. [F] Consolidated profit is shrinking even though revenue grows. PAT fell from Rs 54 crore in FY24 to Rs 44 crore in FY26 and TTM PAT is Rs 39 crore; consolidated OPM fell from 24% (FY24) to 18% (FY26) and 13.2% in Q1 FY27 (NUMBERS). [E] Three-year PAT CAGR is -6.0% against 16.6% sales CAGR (NUMBERS).

2. [F] Capital keeps flowing from the profitable Indian parent into a loss-making chain. The parent has Rs 36.91 crore invested in Control Print BV, loans of Rs 63.68 crore including accrued interest outstanding to it, and Rs 17.84 crore of advances to CP Italy for goods (AR2026 p.179; AR2026 p.197). [F] A further Rs 31.72 crore IP purchase from CP Italy was signed on 8 May 2026 (AR2026 p.199).

3. [F] CP Italy's FY26 loss was Rs 25.16 crore (AR2026 p.70). [E] At the disclosed average rate of Rs 102.51 per euro that is about EUR 2.45 million (AR2026 p.70), against management guidance of EUR 1.0-1.2 million (CALL Nov 2025) and a May 2026 description of about EUR 1.5 million (CALL May 2026).

4. [F] Breakeven targets keep moving. In November 2025 Italy was to break even in FY27 (CALL Nov 2025); in February 2026, in Q3-Q4 FY27 (CALL Feb 2026); in July 2026 the packaging business as a whole 'would probably only break even in the first half of next financial year' (CALL Jul 2026).

5. [F] The foreign subsidiaries' accounts used in consolidation are unaudited: they were 'translated and presented to us by the Holding Company's management and certified by their respective directors' (AR2026 p.207).

6. [F] Standalone profit is flattered by intra-group income: Rs 5.78 crore of interest charged to Control Print BV at 12% (AR2026 p.196), of which Rs 4.99 crore of interest receivable was overdue for more than 90 days (AR2026 p.155).

7. [F] Promoter pay is high: the Chairman and MD received Rs 8.65 crore including an Rs 8 crore commission, 188 times the median employee (AR2026 p.126; AR2026 p.134). [E] Directors' commission equals about 18% of FY26 consolidated PAT of Rs 43.6 crore (AR2026 p.193; AR2026 p.212).

8. [F] Cash conversion is weak in years without one-offs. CFO was Rs 50 crore in each of FY24-FY26 while EBITDA rose from Rs 86 crore to Rs 89 crore; inventory days rose from 224 to 271 in FY26 (NUMBERS).

9. [F] Disclosure is inconsistent. The annual report says CRISIL 'revised' its rating to A/Stable (AR2026 p.140), but CRISIL's own rationale shows the rating sat at 'BB/Stable Issuer Not Cooperating' from 31 December 2025 until 8 July 2026, when it was moved back to A and withdrawn at the company's request (RATING).

10. [E] Valuation already prices a lot: even the bull-case DCF value of Rs 369.2 per share is 40.3% below the price of Rs 618, and the reverse DCF implies about 67.5% annual sales growth for five years (NUMBERS).

[AI] Is the core better than the reported consolidated numbers? Bull: standalone EBITDA margin was 24.7% in FY26 (PPT Jul 2026). Bear: part of standalone profit is interest booked on loans to a loss-making subsidiary chain (AR2026 p.196), so the 'clean core' is slightly overstated.

[AI] Is CP Italy a write-off waiting to happen or an option? Bull: patents to 2036 and to 2044 on recyclable formats (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Nov 2025). Bear: machines are still not standardised. Management said 'We're not through with the machine challenges' (CALL Jul 2026), and older V-Shapes machines mostly sit idle (CALL Jul 2026).

[AI] Will Track and Trace scale? Bull: the draft rule could take QR coding from about 2,000 to about 25,000 SKUs (CALL Jul 2026). Bear: the rule is still a discussion paper, and pilot contracts promised for Q4 FY26 (CALL Feb 2026) were still in evaluation in July 2026 (CALL Jul 2026).

[AI] Is Q1 FY27 a blip? Bull: Q1 is seasonally weak and extrusion demand was hit by polymer volatility (CALL Jul 2026). Bear: consolidated revenue grew only 3.8% while gross margin fell 255 bps year on year (PPT Jul 2026), and input-cost increases are described as 'sticky' (CALL Jul 2026).

[AI] Is the market mispricing the stock? The reverse DCF says the price needs far more growth than history (NUMBERS). The market may instead be capitalising standalone earnings and treating the subsidiaries as a temporary drag. Our DCF model does not support that reading at a 15% WACC.

blocks.text: [AI] Our view is that the Indian coding and marking franchise is real and probably durable. The investment question is capital allocation, not franchise quality. Roughly Rs 118 crore of parent capital ([E] Rs 36.91 crore equity in Control Print BV plus Rs 63.68 crore of loans and interest plus Rs 17.84 crore of advances to CP Italy; AR2026 p.179, p.197) is tied up in a chain whose largest unit has negative equity of about Rs 47 crore ([E] AR2026 p.70). The Rs 31.72 crore IP purchase in FY27 adds to that (AR2026 p.199). None of this is impaired in the parent's books (AR2026 p.179). The market's attention is on the quarterly margin dip. The more important variable is whether the board stops funding the packaging venture if the H1 FY28 breakeven target slips again. Until that is visible, standalone multiples are not the right anchor.

[AI] The Indian coding and marking business is 35 years old. Every growth initiative outside it is less than four years old: Markprint (2022), V-Shapes (JV December 2022, assets March 2024), Codeology (February 2024), MEA (January 2025). Five acquisitions or new entities in about 30 months have turned a single-segment Indian manufacturer into an eight-subsidiary group across five countries. [F] The MD&A itself describes 'a multi-entity, multi-geography structure that has grown considerably in complexity over the past three years' (AR2026 p.51). [AI] The track record that supports the bull case belongs to the old business; the businesses carrying the narrative have no full-cycle history.

blocks.text: [AI] Value is captured in consumables and service, not in the hardware. [MC] Management targets about 60% gross margin and 30% EBIT margin in standalone coding and marking excluding new-venture spending (CALL Jul 2026), and cited 85% margin on a delayed Rs 5 crore of consumable sales (CALL Jul 2026). [F] Standalone gross margin was 59.0% in FY26 (PPT Jul 2026).

[F] Capex has been Rs 8-42 crore a year, 3.9-12.3% of sales over FY17-FY26 (NUMBERS). [MC] Coding and marking needs no major capex because plants run at about 65-70% of capacity (CALL Feb 2026). [AI] The core is moderately asset-light in fixed assets but heavy in working capital: the cash conversion cycle was 283 days in FY26 (NUMBERS). [F] The company outsources some component manufacture to local vendors to save foreign exchange (AR2026 p.71); the extent of outsourcing is not quantified.

blocks.text: [AI] The rising foreign share is acquisition mix, not export strategy: parent exports remain below 3% of turnover. summary.one_line: Control Print's Indian coding and marking franchise is durable and cash-generative, but its profits are being used to fund a loss-making, unaudited Italian packaging venture that keeps missing its milestones, and at Rs 618 the shares trade above even the bull-case DCF value of Rs 369.2.
bull_points: [F] About 85% of coding and marking revenue is recurring aftermarket: consumables 61%, spares 9%, services 15% in FY26 (CALL May 2026).
[F] Standalone operating revenue grew 15.7% to Rs 445.95 crore in FY26 (AR2026 p.49), with standalone EBITDA margin held at 23.8-25.6% over FY21-FY26 (PPT Jul 2026).
[F] The balance sheet is ungeared: debt/equity 0.02 (NUMBERS) and bank-limit use about 27% (RATING).
[E] Losses are concentrated in one unit: CP Italy lost Rs 25.16 crore in FY26 (AR2026 p.70), so a fix would lift consolidated PBT by roughly that amount.
[MC] Track and Trace is already about Rs 20 crore of revenue at breakeven, with upside if the draft pharma QR mandate extends from about 2,000 to about 25,000 SKUs (CALL Jul 2026).
bear_points: [F] Consolidated PAT fell from Rs 54 crore (FY24) to Rs 44 crore (FY26) and Rs 39 crore TTM, and OPM fell from 24% to 13.2% in Q1 FY27, while CFO has been flat at about Rs 50 crore for three years (NUMBERS).

[F] About Rs 118 crore of parent capital is exposed to Control Print BV and CP Italy, unimpaired, while CP Italy has negative net worth of about Rs 47 crore (AR2026 p.70; AR2026 p.179; AR2026 p.197); a further Rs 31.7 crore IP buy-back was signed in May 2026 (AR2026 p.199).

[F] New-venture guidance has slipped on every call: the CP Italy FY26 loss came in at about EUR 2.45 million against EUR 1.0-1.2 million guided ([E] AR2026 p.70; CALL Nov 2025), and packaging breakeven moved out to H1 FY28 (CALL Jul 2026).
